properties.name: MEASURED 2026-10-03: a --serve-shared daemon spawned by a --shared session keeps every file descriptor its parent left open (spawn_daemon sets only stdin/stdout/stderr) — two daemons from a failed test run held a flock(1) lock for 15 minutes and stopped every guarded build on the machine
properties.statement: OBSERVED on the shared build box: tests run as `flock <lock> cargo test …` spawned --shared clients whose daemons (target/debug/reflow2-mcp --graph-path .reflow2/graph --serve-shared) outlived their failed tests; lsof showed both holding the lock file on fd 3, inherited from flock through cargo and the test binary, so every other `flock <lock>` waited until they were killed by hand. A daemon is meant to be detached: shared.rs gives it its own process group and null/log stdio, but Command does not close inherited descriptors above 2, and a daemon lives for --idle-timeout (120 minutes by default). Any descriptor a launcher leaves open — a lock, a pipe whose reader waits for EOF, a socket — is held that long. WORKAROUND used: `flock -o` (closes the lock before running the command). NOT FIXED (outside item 1b): closing descriptors above 2 in the child before exec, or opening with CLOEXEC where reflow2 owns them, would make detachment complete.
